question: Should generic transient tool-progress intent become a public Plugin SDK reply-payload contract?
rationale: The branch creates durable external API surface and a named metadata value; tests cannot determine whether this is the intended long-term plugin contract.

options.title: Accept the generic contract
options.body: Keep the public constant and predicate with narrow transient-only semantics, focused contract coverage, and exact-head Slack proof.

options.title: Keep the seam internal
options.body: Move progress intent to a private bundled-plugin boundary while preserving Slack's typed suppression behavior.

recommendation.title: Accept the generic contract
recommendation.body: Keep the public constant and predicate with narrow transient-only semantics, focused contract coverage, and exact-head Slack proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history signal spans the Plugin SDK, Slack delivery, and Codex integration surfaces involved in this API decision.
